page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.12xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz, delivering 48 dedicated physical cores across 48 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. Hardware cache architecture consists of 64 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache per core, alongside a 36 MB shared L3 cache. The instance features 192.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Networking capabilities provide a 150 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent storage.

Synthetic testing highlights exceptional parallelism and memory throughput across the 48 dedicated ARM cores. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core performance (24039.0), Clang software compilation (71201.0), and PassMark database operations (47761.21). Large-block memory transfers achieve 435.08 GB/sec in read and 216.67 GB/sec in write bandwidth, placing the subsystem in the top ten percent of evaluated instances. Static web serving reaches 98.12 GB/sec, accompanied by 99.18 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics remain moderate, with average scores across Geekbench single-core (1893.0) and stress-ng tests, indicating that aggregate throughput relies on multi-threaded parallel execution rather than individual core velocity.

Resource efficiency is favorable for workloads that distribute tasks across dedicated ARM cores while utilizing high network capacity. The lack of hyperthreading eliminates noisy-neighbor contention across virtual threads. Primary tradeoffs center on the absence of bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures, and the necessity of arm64 binary compatibility. The instance is well suited for large-scale Clang and GCC software build pipelines, static content delivery, in-memory caching nodes, high-concurrency web tiers, and containerized microservice deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.12xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz. Configured on the Nitro System, it provides 48 dedicated physical cores with 48 vCPUs, completely avoiding simultaneous multithreading, alongside 192.0 GB of system memory at a balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio. The platform delivers a 150 Gbps baseline network interface, while omitting integrated local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute, high-throughput software compilation, and large-block memory read bandwidth exceeding 435 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput also place in the upper performance percentiles, though single-core performance remains average. Because persistent storage relies entirely on external EBS volumes, the instance trades local disk IOPS for massive network and memory throughput. It provides a balanced compute-to-memory profile ideal for distributed caching tiers, container orchestration nodes, Clang software builds, and high-concurrency web applications.
